brief.headline: Force Opus to prove its work before you sleep
brief.summary:
Two new tools make an unattended Opus task show proof before it calls itself done. Fablize is a Claude Code plugin that requires completion evidence and passed verification on any Opus task run away from the keyboard. Fable-method ships the same idea as loadable skills, with a think/act/prove eval you can run against a finished task. Install one tonight, so tomorrow's PR review checks proof, not a claim. Separately, OpenCode v1.18.20 stops subagent permission prompts from stalling an overnight run and makes failed subagents resumable — a plain upgrade worth doing regardless of harness.

On cost, route background subagent work to local or open models: opencodex proxies Claude Code and Codex CLI calls to Ollama, Gemini, Grok, and DeepSeek, so only the parts that need Claude use Claude. AT&T reports cutting coding costs 56% by routing 40% of usage to open models, with only a 2% quality drop at 45B tokens a day — a real number to test against your own subagent routing. Put a hard turn or dollar cap on any setup where agents check each other's work: one dev burned $40 in a night when two agents fell into a mutual fact-checking loop. For control away from the desk, devspace bridges Claude Code to the Claude Web app on your phone.
bullets: Install fivetaku/fablize on any unattended Opus task to require completion evidence and verification before it's marked done
Load Sahir619/fable-method's think/act/prove skills and eval to check a finished task's work
Update OpenCode to v1.18.20 to stop subagent permission prompts from stalling overnight runs and to resume failed subagents by task_id
Set a hard turn or spend cap before letting agents cross-verify each other — one dev lost $40 in a night to a mutual fact-checking loop
Point a background subagent at lidge-jun/opencodex to run it on Ollama, Gemini, Grok, or DeepSeek instead of Claude
Use Waishnav/devspace to start and steer a Claude Code task from Claude Web on your phone

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering ships CLI tools — loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost — for designing and orchestrating unattended AI coding-agent loops.
items.whyItMatters: Named commands for auditing and costing agent loops mean you don't have to hand-roll your own harness around Claude Code worktrees/subagents.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering, run loop-init to scaffold a loop, then loop-audit against an existing long-running agent run.

items.title: Leutenegger/book-to-skill — Turn any technical book PDF into a Claude Code skill — ready to study, reference, and use while you work.
items.tldr: Book-to-skill converts any technical book PDF into a Claude Code skill you can reference while you work.
items.whyItMatters: You can turn a manual you already own into a lookup skill instead of re-explaining it to the agent every session.
items.tryThis: Run Leutenegger/book-to-skill against one reference PDF you use often and load the resulting skill into Claude Code.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: Fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus to produce completion evidence and pass verification before it calls a task done.
items.whyItMatters: This makes an unattended agent prove its work before you review the PR, not just claim it finished.
items.tryThis: Install fivetaku/fablize and require it on any Opus task that runs while you are away from the keyboard.

items.title: v1.18.20
items.tldr: OpenCode v1.18.20 makes subagent failures resumable with a task_id, retries more network-error variants, and answers permission prompts triggered by subagents mid-run.
items.whyItMatters: These are the failure modes that stall an overnight run. Upgrading lowers the chance you wake up to a stuck session.
items.tryThis: Update OpenCode to v1.18.20 and check that permission requests from subagents no longer block a run overnight.

items.title: How do you handle insane token costs when letting agents run autonomously?
items.tldr: A dev burned $40 in one night after two of three autonomous research agents fell into an endless mutual fact-checking loop.
items.whyItMatters: Unbounded agent-to-agent verification is a real, reported cost sink in unattended multi-agent runs, not a hypothetical.
items.tryThis: Add a hard turn/spend cap (a hook or wrapper that kills the run past N iterations or $X) before letting agents cross-verify each other unattended.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: Opencodex adds a universal proxy so Codex CLI, Codex App, and Claude Code can call Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, or local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: You can route cheap or local models to background subagents and save Claude for the parts of the job that need it.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point one subagent's model config at a local Ollama model.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: Devspace lets you drive Codex from the ChatGPT web app, or Claude Code from the Claude Web app.
items.whyItMatters: You get a phone-friendly chat bridge to your coding agent without opening a terminal.
items.tryThis: Install Waishnav/devspace and start a Claude Code task from Claude Web on your phone.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: Fable-method distills the Claude Fable 5 workflow into skills any model can run, plus an eval that checks the work.
items.whyItMatters: It gives you a concrete think/act/prove structure to enforce verification before an agent calls a task done.
items.tryThis: Drop the fable-method skills into your Claude Code skills folder and run its eval against a finished task.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: Open-connector is an open-source auth gateway that connects over 1000 SaaS providers to AI agents through MCP, SDK, CLI, and HTTP.
items.whyItMatters: It removes the manual OAuth setup that normally blocks an agent from reaching third-party services while you are asleep.
items.tryThis: Point one MCP-based subagent at open-connector to authenticate a SaaS tool it needs for an overnight task.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: Moli is a headless browser for AI agents, built in Rust for speed and compatibility.
items.whyItMatters: A faster, more reliable browser tool cuts one common source of hangs when a subagent browses or scrapes during an unattended run.
items.tryThis: Swap your agent's browser-automation tool call for lexmount/moli in one workflow and compare hang rate.

items.title: Show HN: Huzzah – a novel approach to coding with AI
items.tldr: Huzzah is a new editor built after its author grew exhausted writing full sentences for every change to coding agents.
items.whyItMatters: This is a first-person account of the same agent fatigue you are trying to engineer away. It is early, but worth watching.
items.tryThis: Read the Huzzah Show HN thread and try the editor on one small task.

items.title: Vomit: Clean up Claude 5's token output with a separate LLM
items.tldr: Vomit runs a separate LLM as a cleanup pass over Claude 5's raw token output before you read it.
items.whyItMatters: A cheap second model can strip verbosity from an agent's output, so your morning review takes less time.
items.tryThis: Add a small local model as a post-process filter on your agent's output before it lands in the PR description.

items.title: not much happened today
items.tldr: AT&T says routing 40% of employee AI usage to open models cut coding costs 56% with only a 2% quality drop at 45B tokens/day, while GPT-5.6 Sol and GitHub Copilot/VS Code get steep price cuts.
items.whyItMatters: Concrete evidence that tiering routine coding work to open-weight models cuts spend with minimal quality loss, plus a fresh price cut worth checking against your current subagent routing.
items.tryThis: Check current GPT-5.6 Sol and Copilot/VS Code pricing, and route low-stakes subagent work to an open model to test AT&T's cost/quality tradeoff yourself.

clusters.title: Enforcing proof-of-work on unattended Opus tasks
clusters.summary: Fablize and fable-method both distill the Claude Fable 5 workflow into a requirement that an agent produce completion evidence and pass verification before it calls a task done.

clusters.title: Cutting agent spend by routing to open/local models
clusters.summary: Opencodex gives you the proxy to send subagent calls to local or open-weight models, and AT&T's reported 56% cost cut at 40% routing is the evidence that it's worth doing.
